question.problem: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$ where $F(x,y)=(3xy-1)\,i+(3{x}^{2}+{e}^{y})\,j$ and $C$ is the boundary of the region enclosed by the curves $y=2x$ and $y={x}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223852/assets/5f34ac74599937e0ae181126ff9a3da5b29dfe213614a1f23ca10c7062f22f7d.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}(3xy-1)\,dx+(3{x}^{2}+{e}^{y})\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=3xy-1$ and $Q(x,y)=3{x}^{2}+{e}^{y}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=3x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =6x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 2x\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(3xy-1)\,dx+(3{x}^{2}+{e}^{y})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(6x-3x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2x}3x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3x[y]_{{x}^{2}}^{2x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3x(2x-{x}^{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3})\,dx \\  & ={[2{x}^{3}-\frac{3{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2(2)^{3}-\frac{3(2)^{4}}{4} \\  & =16-12 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
